ai.title: runTerminalCommand truncates stderr output
ai.summary: The `runTerminalCommand` tool now applies `truncateStringWithMessage` to `stderr`, matching existing `stdout` handling. This prevents oversized error streams from bypassing `COMMAND_OUTPUT_LIMIT` constraints in `sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts`. The change ensures consistent output size enforcement across both streams within the SDK.

eli5.text: If you run a terminal command and it produces a long error message, that error output now gets cut down to the same size limit as the normal output, so you see a shortened version instead of the full wall of text. This only affects the error messages shown through the assistant's built-in command tool, keeping things readable and consistent. The fix is live today.

ai.title: Add base2 variants with task-researcher-full
ai.summary: Added three new agent definition files: `.agents/base2/base2-gpt-5-with-task-researcher.ts`, `.agents/base2/base2-with-task-researcher-full.ts`, and `.agents/researcher/task-researcher-full.ts`. These introduce `Buffy the Orchestrator` variants using `openai/gpt-5` and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5` that spawn `task-researcher` or `task-researcher-full` as the first layer for context gathering. The new `task-researcher-full` extends the base researcher with a structured output schema requiring a facts-only `report` and `relevantFiles` list, enforcing a multi-layer research workflow before editing.

eli5.text: The coding assistant now has an optional helper it can send out first to read the relevant files and gather facts before it starts planning or editing. That helper is required to hand back a written report of just the facts and a list of the files it examined, so the main assistant works from a focused, pre-filtered set of information instead of rummaging through the whole codebase itself. This new "research-first" option is in place today for teams using the GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 orchestrator variants.

ai.title: Skip terminal command detection for SDK
ai.summary: Added `!fingerprintId.startsWith('codebuff-sdk-')` guard to terminal command detection logic in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. Prevents `checkTerminalCommand` execution for SDK sessions, avoiding unnecessary processing. Internal change; no user-facing impact yet.

eli5.text: Internal software used to check whether you were running a direct terminal command has been told to skip that check when the session belongs to the SDK line. The change is live today in the backend, but because no external behavior was added, most people won't notice anything. Developers working on SDK-integrated flows will see one fewer unnecessary processing step when their sessions run.

ai.title: Move quickjs-sandbox to agent-runtime
ai.summary: Relocates `quickjs-sandbox.ts` from `backend/src/util/` to `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/`. Updates `backend/src/run-programmatic-step.ts` to import `SandboxManager` from `@codebuff/agent-runtime/util/quickjs-sandbox`. Scope limited to file move and import path adjustment.

eli5.text: The assistant's sandbox component, which lets it safely run code snippets, was moved from one part of the codebase to the agent runtime package. This is a behind-the-scenes organizational change that makes future improvements easier to plan and maintain. Nothing about how the assistant works changes today, but the move sets up better structure for upcoming enhancements to the agent runtime.

ai.title: Nightly buffbench evals switch to grok-4-fast and lower concurrency
ai.summary: Nightly buffbench evaluation configuration updated in evals/buffbench/main-nightly.ts to run 'base' and 'base-lite-grok-4-fast' agents, replacing 'base2'. Task concurrency reduced from 20 to 5 to manage load or rate limits. This change affects the internal nightly evaluation pipeline for buffbench.

eli5.text: Every night, the system runs a set of automated tests called 'buffbench evaluations' to check how well the coding assistant performs at different tasks. The engineers changed which assistant version is being tested, they swapped out the 'base2' version for a faster version called 'grok-4-fast', and they also reduced how many tasks run at the same time from 20 down to 5. If you looked at these nightly reports, you'd now see results from the faster version instead of the old one, and it might take a bit longer to finish all the tests because fewer are running in parallel.

ai.title: SDK build script uses fs.rm() instead of execSync rm -rf
ai.summary: Replaced `execSync('rm -rf dist')` with `await rm('dist', { recursive: true, force: true })` in `sdk/scripts/build.ts`. This change ensures cross-platform compatibility for cleaning the dist directory, removing reliance on Unix-specific shell commands. The update affects the SDK build process only.

eli5.text: The assistant's software-building kit now cleans up old files before creating new ones using a method that works the same way on Windows, Mac, and Linux computers, instead of using a command that only works on Unix-based systems like Mac and Linux. This means anyone building or using the kit on a Windows machine will no longer run into problems during the setup process. The change is small and only affects people working directly with the kit's build process, not everyday users.

ai.title: base2-fast mode added; find-all-referencer model bump
ai.summary: New `base2-fast.ts` defines `Buffy the Fast Orchestrator` via `createBase2('fast')`. `base2.ts` updates `createBase2` signature to accept `'normal' | 'fast'`, gating plan/validator agent spawning in fast mode. `base2-alloy.ts` switches from `'max'` to `'normal'`. `find-all-referencer.ts` model changes from `x-ai/grok-code-fast-1` to `x-ai/grok-4-fast`. `base2-simple.ts` renames spawned agents `file-picker` to `file-picker-max` and `reviewer` to `code-reviewer`, adds explicit plan step. `knowledge.md` removes `exec` runner instructions.

eli5.text: A new faster mode was added to the internal agent orchestration system, letting a lightweight version of the assistant skip extra planning steps and move straight to getting things done. The system also updated the underlying AI model used for searching code references, and renamed a couple of internal helper steps to clearer names. Additionally, outdated instructions for running services locally were removed from the project knowledge base. These changes are live for internal use, affecting how the assistant behaves when operating in the new fast configuration.

ai.title: Move live-user-inputs to agent-runtime
ai.summary: Live user input state moved to `packages/agent-runtime`. Functions now accept `params` objects with injected state instead of module-level globals. Backend imports updated to use `@codebuff/agent-runtime/live-user-inputs`. WebSocket server passes `sessionConnections` from `BACKEND_AGENT_RUNTIME_IMPL`.

eli5.text: When two people open the same assistant conversation at the same time, the assistant now reliably stops the older session instead of letting both run. Previously the list of active conversations was kept in one place and shared by whoever asked first, so it could get mixed up; that list now lives inside the engine that runs the assistant and is passed in fresh to each session. If you open a conversation that someone else is already using, your new request quietly takes over and the earlier one stops responding. The change is live now.

ai.title: Fix typecheck in base2-hybrid-max agent
ai.summary: Changed createBase2 argument from 'max' to 'normal' in .agents/base2/base2-hybrid-max.ts. Resolves typecheck error by aligning base2 initialization with expected parameter type. Internal agent definition update.

eli5.text: The assistant configuration labeled as 'max' was quietly switched to use a different underlying mode. Anyone running that specific helper setup will now be using standard settings instead of maximum ones, though the change is purely internal and nothing visible should behave differently. This is already live in the current code.

ai.title: Inject addAgentStep into run-programmatic-step
ai.summary: Refactored `runProgrammaticStep` to accept `addAgentStep` as an injected dependency instead of importing it directly from `./agent-run`. This change updates the function signature to include `AddAgentStepFn` and modifies internal calls to use the passed-in parameter, ensuring consistent dependency injection patterns across the backend. The update affects `backend/src/run-programmatic-step.ts` and requires callers to provide the `addAgentStep` function.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs a step in a task, it used to fetch a helper tool directly from a fixed location inside its own code. Now that helper is handed to it from outside instead, so the step-runner no longer assumes where the helper comes from. This is purely behind-the-scenes plumbing, you won't see any difference in how tasks run, and only the internal development team felt the effect today.

ai.title: Move custom-file-picker-config to agent-runtime
ai.summary: Relocates `custom-file-picker-config.ts` from `backend/src/find-files/` to `packages/agent-runtime/src/find-files/`. Updates imports in `request-files-prompt.ts` to use the new `@codebuff/agent-runtime` path. This aligns file picker configuration with the agent runtime package boundaries.

eli5.text: The team moved the file picker configuration code from the main backend into the agent runtime package, and updated the request files prompt module to import it from the new location instead of the local path. This is a behind-the-scenes housekeeping change that reorganizes code to match the intended package boundaries, with no direct user-facing behavior changes. The file itself was essentially relocated without any modifications.

ai.title: Move gemini-with-fallbacks to agent-runtime
ai.summary: Relocated `gemini-with-fallbacks.ts` from `backend/src/llm-apis/` to `packages/agent-runtime/src/llm-api/`. Updated imports in `fast-rewrite.ts` and `request-files-prompt.ts` to reference the new `@codebuff/agent-runtime` path. This consolidates LLM API logic within the agent-runtime package.

eli5.text: The assistant moved a shared piece of its behind-the-scenes text-handling logic into one centralized location used by other parts of the system. If you were to open the project, you would see the file now lives alongside other similar helper tools rather than in a separate folder. Two files that rely on this logic now load it from the central location, so the change is live today, even though you wouldn't notice anything different while using the assistant.

ai.title: Remove custom file picker logic from request-files-prompt
ai.summary: Deleted `getCustomFilePickerConfigForOrg` and associated schema imports from `backend/src/find-files/request-files-prompt.ts`. The function previously fetched org-specific file picker configs from the database, but its call site was already hard-coded to return `null`. `requestRelevantFiles` now uses the static `MAX_FILES_PER_REQUEST` constant directly, removing dead code paths for custom model selection and max-file overrides.

eli5.text: Some behind-the-scenes code that could let organizations use a customized file picker, one that pulled special settings from a database, has been removed, even though those database lookups had already been disabled for a while. This just cleans house by deleting the leftover, unused logic, so the system now always falls back to its standard way of picking relevant files. Nothing you do changes as a result; it's internal cleanup with no direct effect on how the assistant behaves.

ai.title: Move request-files-prompt to agent-runtime
ai.summary: Move request-files-prompt.ts from backend/src/find-files to packages/agent-runtime/src/find-files. Update imports in find-files.ts to use @codebuff/agent-runtime/find-files/request-files-prompt. Adjust internal imports within moved file to use relative paths for local agent-runtime modules.

eli5.text: The part of the program that picks out the right files for the assistant to read has been moved into the toolkit that runs the agent. If you watch the assistant in action, nothing about what it does or how fast it works changes; this is just behind-the-scenes rearranging so all those moving pieces live in one place instead of being scattered between two parts of the system.

ai.title: Move getFileReadingUpdates to agent-runtime
ai.summary: Relocated `get-file-reading-updates` from `backend/src` to `packages/agent-runtime/src`. Updated `find-files.ts` and `read-files.ts` to import `getFileReadingUpdates` via `@codebuff/agent-runtime/get-file-reading-updates`. This aligns file reading update logic with the agent runtime package structure.

eli5.text: The assistant's ability to track file-reading progress got relocated within the app's organization, so that the behind-the-scenes logic now lives in a shared folder used by different parts of the system instead of being tucked away in a backend-only space. This is housekeeping: no feature you tap turned on or off today, just a cleaner way for the engineers to maintain that file-reading tracking thing. If you opened the app right now you would notice nothing different; the change only readies the structure for later work.

ai.title: Fix backend unit tests
ai.summary: Corrects type mismatches and missing dependencies in backend unit tests. Imports `TEST_AGENT_RUNTIME_IMPL` and `AgentRuntimeDeps` to properly mock agent runtime behavior. Updates `mockParams` to use `toolCallParams` and `system` instead of deprecated fields, and relaxes strict typing for chunk arrays.

eli5.text: The team fixed a broken set of checks that verify the agent's core logic still works. These checks had been failing because they fed the agent the wrong kind of setup data and expected outdated formats, so the team corrected the fake profiles and field names used during testing. You would not see this yourself, but if you are a developer running these checks, they should now pass instead of erroring out. It is live in the codebase today as a behind-the-scenes fix to keep the agent's behavior reliable.

ai.title: Move render-read-files-result to agent-runtime
ai.summary: Moved parse-tool-call-xml.ts to packages/agent-runtime/src/util/render-read-files-result.ts. Updated imports in find-files.ts and read-files.ts to use new path. Refactors tool handler dependencies to shared runtime package.

eli5.text: The assistant's file-reading helpers have been reorganized into a shared toolkit that the main system and its extensions both use, so updates to how file results are displayed only need to be made in one place. This affects the backend system that powers the assistant's file search and reading features, and you'd notice it as smoother, more consistent behavior when those tools report results, no visible new features, just cleaner maintenance work behind the scenes.
